traffic-sign-inspection.title: Street-view GeoAI and asset localization
traffic-sign-inspection.summary: End-to-end GeoAI pipeline for detection and geospatial localization of 130 traffic sign and 33 street furniture classes from 360° street imagery.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Municipalities and road authorities require accurate, up-to-date inventories of traffic signs, road markings, and roadside furniture. Traditional field surveying is notoriously slow, costly, and hazardous for crews operating along busy arterial roadways. Automated mobile mapping using car-mounted 360° cameras offers high coverage, but manually inspecting millions of panoramic frames creates an insurmountable manual bottleneck.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Engineered a high-throughput deep learning and multi-view triangulation pipeline:

- **Asset Detection & Multi-Class Classification:** Trained custom YOLOv5 models robust to motion blur, occlusions, changing weather, and viewpoint shifts across **130 distinct traffic sign categories** and **33 street furniture classes**.
- **Temporal Tracking & Geospatial Localization:** Coupled visual detections across sequential frames using vehicle trajectory telemetry, GPS/IMU logs, and epipolar triangulation to estimate real-world 3D coordinates.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body:
The deployed GeoAI solution delivered:

- **>95% object detection accuracy** across challenging urban lighting environments.
- **92% geospatial localization precision**, aligning detected assets within sub-meter GIS survey thresholds.
- Eliminated hundreds of hours of manual field inspection, converting raw video logs into structured, GIS-ready asset inventories.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Combining deep convolutional object detectors with rigorous geometric camera projective models provides the optimal bridge between 2D computer vision and production-grade geospatial asset inventories.

building-change.title: Multi-temporal building change detection
building-change.summary: Deep learning change detection system identifying building extensions, new constructions, and demolitions from multi-year orthophotos.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Accurate monitoring of urban sprawl, unpermitted construction, and municipal infrastructure alterations requires comparing high-resolution aerial orthophoto surveys flown across multiple years. Manual photo interpretation across entire regions is slow, expensive, and subject to visual fatigue.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body: Designed convolutional neural network pipelines trained on multi-temporal, high-resolution aerial imagery to distinguish actual structural changes from seasonal variations, differing illumination, vegetation growth, and sensor viewpoints. Integrated the automated detection pipeline into an interactive GIS-based web validation platform for cartographic reviewers.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Achieved **88% detection accuracy** across varied urban and peri-urban landscapes, reducing manual inspection and verification efforts by **65%**.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Feature-level differential learning combined with robust geometric image pre-registration prevents pseudo-change false alarms caused by solar angle differences and camera orientation.

retinal-oct-dl.title: Retinal OCT Disease Classification with Explainable AI
retinal-oct-dl.summary: Deep learning classification of retinal optical coherence tomography scans using LIME for transparent visual model explanations.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Deep learning models achieve high diagnostic accuracy in classifying retinal conditions—such as Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV), Diabetic Macular Edema (DME), and Drusen—from Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) scans. However, clinical adoption remains heavily bottlenecked by the black-box nature of deep neural networks, where clinicians cannot verify the underlying diagnostic rationale.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body: Implemented transfer learning architectures using deep convolutional backbones and integrated Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME). This technique generates localized super-pixel attribution masks, highlighting the exact anatomical retinal layers and lesion boundaries that drive model predictions.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Validated on benchmark OCT datasets, achieving high diagnostic sensitivity and specificity while providing ophthalmologists with interpretable visual explanations that corroborate recognized clinical biomarkers (published at IEEE CSDE 2021).

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Explainable AI is indispensable for translational medical diagnostics; interpretable attribution maps provide verifiable clinical pathways rather than opaque numeric confidence scores.

orthophoto-production.title: Orthophoto production, pose estimation, and AI QA
orthophoto-production.summary: Automated orthophoto production with AI image quality assessment (97%), PostGIS/AHN seamline optimization, and 2-pixel camera pose estimation.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Production of high-resolution country-wide orthophoto mosaics involves thousands of raw aerial frames. Quality assessment (detecting cloud cover, shadows, blur) and initial camera pose estimation traditionally require extensive manual inspection and tedious tie-point editing.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Architected and implemented AI-based automation tools across the photogrammetric orthophoto production lifecycle:

- **AI-Based Image Quality Assessment (QA):** Developed deep learning models to detect cloud, shadow, and blur artifacts on raw aerial imagery prior to aerial triangulation (AT).
- **Automated Camera Pose Estimation:** Engineered a feature-matching and tie-point generation framework to register incoming flight images against historical reference orthophotos.
- **Elevation-Guided Seamline Optimization:** Automated seamline placement and geometric validation using PostgreSQL/PostGIS paired with AHN airborne LiDAR elevation data.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body:
The automated photogrammetry pipeline achieved:

- **97% QA classification accuracy** for atmospheric defects.
- **2-pixel camera alignment accuracy**, cutting manual aerial triangulation effort by **90%**.
- Reduced manual seamline editing by **65%**.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Injecting computer vision feature matching into classical photogrammetric bundle adjustment removes the most time-consuming manual intervention in large-scale aerial cartography.

gis-digitization.title: Large-scale 3D CityGML modeling and texture projection
gis-digitization.summary: Automated pipeline for 3D CityGML reconstruction and photorealistic texture generation from high-resolution aerial imagery.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Modern municipal digital twins require semantic 3D building models (CityGML) with photorealistic textured facades for urban planning, solar potential modeling, and environmental simulation. Manually projecting aerial imagery onto 3D building meshes is slow and prone to severe perspective distortion and occlusions.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Built an automated pipeline for large-scale 3D CityGML reconstruction and photorealistic texture generation:

- **Automated 3D Reconstruction:** Developed algorithms converting 2D footprint geometries and elevation models into semantic 3D CityGML building representations at scale.
- **Occlusion-Aware Multi-View Texture Projection:** Designed custom texture projection algorithms that dynamically evaluate viewing angles, occlusions, and image resolution to project aerial imagery onto 3D building facades.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Maintained strict geometric alignment with a **texture shift of less than 3 pixels**, generating high-fidelity photorealistic urban digital twin models across municipal districts.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Ray-traced visibility culling is essential when texturing 3D building facades from oblique aerial views to prevent roof overhangs and neighboring structures from projecting false textures.

point-cloud-processing.title: 3D point cloud intelligence and BIM extraction
point-cloud-processing.summary: AI-driven semantic segmentation and BIM model extraction from aerial, mobile, and indoor LiDAR datasets.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Laser scanners generate billions of raw 3D spatial points (LiDAR). Converting these unorganized point clouds into parametric Building Information Modeling (BIM) objects—such as walls, structural columns, and MEP piping systems—has traditionally been a labor-intensive manual CAD tracing process.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Developed point cloud intelligence algorithms for semantic segmentation and automated BIM extraction:

- **Multi-Source LiDAR Processing:** Built processing pipelines handling dense 3D point clouds across diverse acquisition platforms: aerial surveys, mobile vehicle-mounted mapping systems, and high-precision indoor laser scanners.
- **Automated Pipe & Geometry Extraction:** Implemented custom algorithms to detect industrial and building piping networks, segment structural components, and extract geometric properties directly from unstructured 3D point data.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Achieved **95% extraction accuracy** while cutting manual 3D modeling and CAD drafting time by **60%** across complex industrial facility scans.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Combining statistical point cloud spatial clustering with robust geometric primitive fitting provides a scalable foundation for automated scan-to-BIM digital transformation.

remote-sensing.title: Multispectral earth observation and remote sensing AI
remote-sensing.summary: AI solutions using Sentinel satellite imagery for crop classification, water quality analysis, and algae bloom detection (2nd place, international tender).
remote-sensing.track_name: Track 3: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) & Remote Sensing

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Environmental degradation, water pollution, and agricultural resource stress require frequent, wide-area monitoring. Earth observation satellites provide continuous coverage, but transforming raw multispectral radiation bands into actionable environmental intelligence demands automated spectral analytics.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Deployed AI solutions leveraging European Space Agency (ESA) Sentinel-2 multispectral satellite imagery:

- **Multispectral Analytics:** Engineered computer vision pipelines operating across Sentinel-2 optical and infrared spectral bands to analyze vegetative indices (NDVI, EVI), crop phenology, and surface water dynamics.
- **Environmental Monitoring:** Built multi-class deep learning models for automated crop type classification, water body delineation, and harmful algae bloom detection across inland water bodies.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: This Earth observation analytics framework secured **2nd place in an international innovation tender**, demonstrating high-precision surface water quality mapping and agricultural classification.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Exploiting non-visible red-edge and short-wave infrared (SWIR) bands provides vital diagnostic discriminators for environmental and vegetative health that are completely missed by standard RGB imagery.

postgis-seamlines.title: PostGIS & AHN LiDAR Seamline Optimization Pipeline
postgis-seamlines.summary: Automated spatial database pipeline utilizing elevation models to optimize mosaic cutlines, avoiding high-relief structures and cutting manual seamline editing by 65%.
postgis-seamlines.role: AI engineering and spatial database development
postgis-seamlines.track_name: Track 3: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) & Remote Sensing

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: In large-scale aerial orthophoto mosaic generation, seamlines dividing adjacent overlapping flight swaths frequently slice through tall buildings, bridges, and infrastructure. This leads to conspicuous visual shear, duplicate structures, and perspective artifacts across municipal orthophoto deliverables.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body: Engineered an automated spatial database optimization framework integrating PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial operators with AHN (Actueel Hoogtebestand Nederland) airborne LiDAR elevation data. The pipeline calculates cost surfaces based on vertical elevation variance, guiding seamlines through natural ground-level paths (such as roads and open fields) and avoiding elevated structures.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: The automated elevation-guided seamline placement reduced manual cartographic inspection and seamline adjustment by **65%**, while eliminating visible structural shearing across multi-square-kilometer urban surveys.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Integrating high-precision 3D LiDAR height data into relational spatial databases transforms a traditionally laborious manual photogrammetric editing step into a deterministic, scalable spatial computing procedure.

vehicle-detection.title: Multi-Label Vehicle & Traffic Analytics Framework
vehicle-detection.summary: Comparative deep learning benchmark of YOLO and R-CNN architectures across 21 vehicle categories with spatial trajectory analysis.
vehicle-detection.track_name: Track 3: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) & Remote Sensing

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Accurate multi-class vehicle detection and density estimation are critical for intelligent transportation systems (ITS) and traffic flow management. Real-world roadway video streams present challenges of occlusion, high variation in vehicle scale, and variable illumination.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Conducted an extensive empirical evaluation comparing single-stage (YOLOv3, YOLOv5) and two-stage (Faster R-CNN) object detectors trained across **21 distinct vehicle and traffic classes**. Optimized data augmentation pipelines, anchor box distributions, and inference runtimes for edge and server deployment environments.

Code repository: [Multi-Label Vehicle Detection on GitHub](https://github.com/fahome10bd/Multi-Label-Vehicle-detection-based-on-AI).

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Achieved real-time inference speeds with robust detection precision across congested urban roadway scenes, establishing clear trade-off benchmarks between computational latency and spatial bounding-box fidelity.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Single-stage detectors provide the optimal speed-accuracy frontier for real-time edge streaming, while two-stage architectures offer superior recall for heavily occluded small-scale vehicles in dense bottlenecks.

eeg-research.title: Locomotive features in EEG of impaired consciousness
eeg-research.summary: Undergraduate thesis at IUT on analyzing EEG time-series signals and distinctive cerebral rhythms in impaired consciousness (coma).

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Accurately assessing the depth of impaired consciousness in comatose patients is critical for prognostic evaluation and clinical intervention. Conventional bedside clinical assessments (such as the Glasgow Coma Scale) can be subjective, motivating quantitative mathematical analysis of neurophysiological electroencephalogram (EEG) signals.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Investigated in my undergraduate B.Sc. thesis in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at the Islamic University of Technology (IUT):

**"Quantifying Locomotive Features in EEG of Impaired Consciousness (Coma) with Distinctive Cerebral Rhythms"**

- **Signal Pre-Processing & Filtering:** Applied bandpass filtering and artifact rejection to isolate neural oscillations from ocular and myogenic interference.
- **Spectral & Rhythm Decomposition:** Extracted canonical cerebral rhythms (delta, theta, alpha, beta) and evaluated spectral power distributions and temporal rhythm dynamics across patient cohorts.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Demonstrated that distinctive cerebral rhythm transitions correlate with depth of consciousness, establishing quantitative markers for neurological state evaluation. Evaluated under both Project and Thesis courses at IUT, receiving the highest grade of **A+** for research rigor.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Spectral power entropy and delta/alpha power ratios provide robust non-invasive quantitative indicators of cortical depression in impaired consciousness.

fault-detection.title: Automated Machine Fault Detection via Vibration Signal Analysis
fault-detection.summary: Autonomous rule-based fault detection engine processing accelerometer vibration data to diagnose bearing, gear, and mechanical faults without manual intervention.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: Rotating machinery in industrial manufacturing plants is prone to mechanical degradation across bearings, gear meshes, and rotating shafts. Conventional condition monitoring requires skilled vibration analysts to manually inspect Fourier frequency spectra, which is slow, expensive, and difficult to scale to 24/7 automated plant monitoring.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Engineered an autonomous diagnostic rule engine in MATLAB:

- **Order Spectrum Analysis:** Converted time-domain accelerometer vibration signals via Discrete Fourier Transform (FFT) into shaft rotational speed multiples (×RPM orders), normalizing against speed fluctuations.
- **Autonomous Decision Tree:** Formulated a structured decision engine that evaluates spectral energy against healthy baseline thresholds, classifying bearing (inner race, outer race, ball bearing), gear mesh, unbalance, and misalignment defects.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: The autonomous engine accurately diagnosed simulated and experimental mechanical fault conditions without human intervention, maintaining deterministic 100% reproducibility across standard test cases.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Shaft order tracking combined with baseline-normalized harmonic thresholding provides an interpretable, mathematically transparent alternative to opaque neural network classifiers for industrial predictive maintenance.

cmbr-astrophysics.title: CMBR Primordial Signal Isolation & Sky-Map Generation
cmbr-astrophysics.summary: Filtering cosmological noise from fragmented WMAP satellite datasets to isolate primordial radiation and generate clean astronomical sky-maps.

blocks.heading: Problem Description & Context
blocks.body: The Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR) contains the thermal imprint of the infant universe. However, satellite observations (such as NASA WMAP raw sensor feeds) are heavily obscured by bright synchrotron and dust emission from the Milky Way, instrument noise, and fragmented sky coverage.

blocks.heading: Technical Challenges & Approaches
blocks.body:
Implemented statistical signal processing and calibration algorithms in MATLAB to isolate primordial cosmological signals:

- **Multi-Frequency Channel Cleaning:** Processed disparate microwave radiometer feeds to calibrate sensor gain and remove localized instrument offsets.
- **Galactic Noise Suppression:** Applied spatial and statistical filtering algorithms to attenuate high-intensity galactic plane noise while preserving microkelvin primordial temperature anisotropies.

blocks.heading: Effects & Quantitative Results
blocks.body: Successfully generated clean, high-contrast primordial radiation sky-maps from raw observation datasets, revealing subtle temperature anisotropies with high statistical fidelity.

blocks.heading: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
blocks.body: Rigorous spatial signal processing and foreground noise modeling are essential for uncovering subtle primordial cosmological signals embedded in overwhelming galactic interference.
